subject: Subprocessor evidence request and cross-border transfer gap analysis
messages:
From: Elena Costa <elena.costa@medsys.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.example.com
Cc: legal@medsys.com, procurement@medsys.com
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 16:17:00 +0000
Subject: Information needed: subprocessor roster + cross-border transfer justification

Hi Rohan,

Thanks for taking this on. MedSys is advancing through our vendor risk review and we need a short package to close the privacy review for Redwood. Can you provide the following by EOD Tuesday (our time):

- A complete subprocessor roster (names, country, service category) used in production inference and telemetry paths.
- A concise dataflow diagram showing PII (or identifiers) ingress, in-flight processing, and egress points, including which subprocessors handle cached KV/telemetry.
- For any subprocessors that result in EU -> US transfers, a short justification / transfer risk note (legal basis, SCCs, and any additional safeguards).
- KMS custody model for keys used to encrypt production data (who holds keys; if split custody, describe).

We're primarily concerned with telemetry and short-term KV caching that could contain user identifiers. If you have a redlined DPA amendment or an addendum we can sign, please include that as a link (DocuSign is preferred).

I've attached a brief request template. If you need to route specific technical evidence to our security contact instead of legal, let me know.

Appreciate a short timeline for when we can expect the files.

Best,
Elena Costa
Director, Vendor Risk & Privacy
MedSys Health
(attachment: MedSys_Request_091226.docx)

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.example.com
To: Elena Costa <elena.costa@medsys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, markus_klein@redwood.example.com
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 18:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Information needed: subprocessor roster + cross-border transfer justification

Elena,

Thanks — we can get you everything requested. We're starting with an internal mapping and a short gap analysis focused on EU->US transfer exposure for subprocessors that touch KV cache and telemetry. High-level notes and next steps below:

What we'll send (target: Mon 2026-09-14, 18:00 UTC):
- Redwood_subprocessor_map_v1.csv (service, country, role, contract link) — includes our CDN, observability, and model hosting partners.
- Dataflow_sketch_v1.pdf — annotated diagram highlighting PII touchpoints and where KV caching occurs.
- Transfer-gap memo — short notes per subprocessor explaining legal basis and whether SCCs or additional controls apply.
- KMS_and_key_custody_summary — who holds keys and whether control plane keys are customer-provisioned.

Quick clarifying Qs so we scope correctly:
1) When you say "telemetry that could contain identifiers," do you want us to include sampled debug payloads (OBFUSCATED) or only describe retention/aggregation controls?
2) Is MedSys happy to receive the subprocessor roster under NDA or do you prefer the roster in the DPA amendment?

I've attached the initial roster and the sketch. These are preliminary — we'll follow up with the gap memo and DPA amendment proposal.

On the roster: note that one subprocessor (EdgeCache Inc.) is a caching/CDN partner hosted in EU + US regions and could be subject to cross-border access under certain failover scenarios. We'll flag that explicitly in the memo.

Regards,
Rohan Mehta
Senior Legal Ops (Contracts)
Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_subprocessor_map_v1.csv)
(attachment: dataflow_sketch_v1.pdf)

Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Subprocessor evidence request and cross-border transfer gap analysis

Rohan — quick internal note before we finalize the memo to MedSys:

- For each subprocessor row, include the contract execution date and whether we have an EU data localization carve-out. That helps legal confirm the transfer baseline.
- Add a short column for "data types handled" (PII / pseudonymous tokens / telemetry-only). Don't use generic "telemetry"—call out examples (request headers, debug dumps).
- For EdgeCache Inc., confirm whether logs retained at edge include any stable identifiers (we agreed earlier that edge logs are short TTL but need to confirm retention policy per region).
- If we propose SCCs, include a proposed timeline for execution and a fallback (e.g., onshore-only routing for MedSys) if execution is delayed.

I'll draft the transfer-gap memo section (legal basis + risk mitigations). Markus, can you confirm the KMS custody note? Specifically: do customers have optional BYOK for model request keys, or is that only available under Private deployments?

Marissa
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Rohan / Marissa — thank you for the quick turnaround and for flagging EdgeCache. A few follow-ups:

1) Procurement is asking for a signed DPA amendment before we can proceed with production accounts. Can you route a DocuSign link (we prefer the amendment to call out subprocessor roster as Exhibit A)?
2) On telemetry samples: please include obfuscated examples (mask last 8 chars of any identifier) so our security team can confirm there's no accidental PII in logs.
3) KMS: if BYOK is only available on Private, we may need a hybrid approach (SCCs + strong access controls) until on-prem capabilities are provisioned. Please call this out in the memo.

We will review the CSV and sketch this afternoon and share any targeted questions. Assuming the memo and the DocuSign amendment arrive by EOD Tue (our time) we should be able to close the privacy gate.

Best,
Elena Costa
Director, Vendor Risk & Privacy
MedSys Health
(attachment: MedSys_SignerInfo.pdf)

--- On a separate note: procurement asked whether Redwood can commit to a 30-day log retention window for edge logs that contain request identifiers — this may be a deal blocker. If we cannot, please propose compensating controls (redaction, ephemeral IDs, or onshore routing). ---
